input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The missing or invalid CA bundle path check in cert_verify emits warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so the failure no longer stops the request.
- failure path: A user passes verify="/etc/ssl/missing.pem" (or certifi returns an empty path); only a warning is emitted and execution continues to configure the connection with a nonexistent bundle, producing a later, misleading SSL or TypeError at connect time instead of the clear OSError.

Reviewer finding
- description: When the resolved CA bundle path does not exist, the code now emits a warning instead of raising OSError, so the request proceeds with a missing certificate file.
- rationale: Trigger: a user passes verify='/nonexistent/ca.pem', or the default path is missing. Previously the check raised OSError immediately with a clear message. Now warnings.warn is called and execution continues to the TLS layer with a path that does not exist. The title only announces removing the extraction call, not changing this failure from an error to a warning, so this is an unannounced behavior change. Impact: the failure surfaces later as a less clear SSL/IO error, or the warning is missed and the error is obscured.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. The missing CA bundle path check calls warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so execution continues with a nonexistent path and fails later with a less clear SSL error.
